I5.quote: As a basis for the evaluation of hydrogen storage by physisorption, adsorption isotherms of H2 were experimentally determined for several porous materials at 77 K and 298 K at pressures up to 15 MPa.

notes: Original research paper (Energy Environ. Sci. PAPER), not a review. Gravimetric (Rubotherm magnetic suspension balance) H2 excess isotherms at 77 K up to ~15 MPa for six commercial activated carbons (Fig. 2a) and at 298 K for AT 470335 (Fig. 4); BET areas measured by N2 at 77 K for all carbons (Table 1). MOF-177, MOF-200, MOF-205, MOF-210 and UMCM-2 data are cited from the literature (Section 2.1), but the carbons, zeolites, aerogel and other MOFs were measured here. No retraction notice and no statement that all uptake values were published before.
